problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to perform maintenance at five critical facilities scattered across a region. The geographical positions of these facilities are recorded as follows:

Facility Alpha: Coordinates (134,70)
Facility Beta: Coordinates (133,60)
Facility Gamma: Coordinates (55,173)
Facility Delta: Coordinates (150,107)
Facility Epsilon: Coordinates (148,70)

Travel distances between facilities, measured in kilometers, are precomputed and known:
Alpha to Gamma: 129.8 km
Alpha to Delta: 40.3 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 14.0 km
Beta to Gamma: 137.3 km
Beta to Delta: 50.0 km
Beta to Epsilon: 18.0 km
Gamma to Delta: 115.7 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 138.8 km
Delta to Epsilon: 37.1 km

Due to geographical obstructions, no direct service route exists between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta. Furthermore, a routing directive mandates that the final itinerary must incorporate exactly one, but not both, of the following two possible connections: the link between Facility Beta and Facility Gamma, or the link between Facility Gamma and Facility Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-circuit inspection tour, where the technician visits each facility precisely one time before returning to the origin point, thereby minimizing the total travel distance.
